repair_notes.mathematical_evidence: For a bounded stopping time rho and fixed 0<t<=T, round rho wedge t upward on {kt/2^r:0<=k<=2^r}. Each cell event is F_q-measurable at its grid endpoint q<=t; hence each stopped Brownian approximation is F_t-measurable. Define Z_t by the finite vector limit, and zero where it fails. On the common continuity event, Z_t=W_(rho wedge t). For every Borel C, {W_rho in C} intersect {rho<=t} differs from {Z_t in C} intersect {rho<=t} only within the ambient null continuity complement, every subset of which is in F_0 under the usual conditions. This proves each stopped test; t=0 uses W_0 and t=T also proves ambient measurability. This is precisely the cited supplier argument with its actual necessary hypotheses, rather than an application of its narrower Statement. It works coordinatewise and adds no choice principle.
